/25 Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.128

128 addresses · 126 usable hosts · wildcard 0.0.0.127

CIDR notation

Subnet mask

0.0.0.127

Binary mask
11111111.11111111.11111111.10000000
Host bits
7

What a /25 means

A /25 gives 126 usable hosts, which fits small VLANs such as servers, voice, guest Wi-Fi or a small branch.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /25 uses 25 network bits and leaves 7 host bits, so the block contains 128 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−25) − 2 = 128 − 2 = 126.

Example /25 blocks inside 192.168.1.0/24

NetworkUsable rangeBroadcast
192.168.1.0/25192.168.1.1 – 192.168.1.126192.168.1.127
192.168.1.128/25192.168.1.129 – 192.168.1.254192.168.1.255

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.128
!
access-list 10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.127

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.1/25

Linux

ip addr add 192.168.1.1/25 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /25?

126. A /25 has 128 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 126 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /25?

255.255.255.128. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.0.127.
